newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian official confirms wartime trophy art vote.
newsitem.headline: Russian official confirms wartime trophy art vote.

text.p: Russia's deputy culture minister confirmed on Tuesday that parliament had overruled Boris Yeltsin's veto on a bill asserting Moscow's ownership of art works seized from Nazi Germany during World War Two.

Mikhail Shvydkoi said he did not know the exact voting figure in the upper house but told Reuters that about 140 members -- well over the required two thirds of the Federation Council -- had cast written ballots to overrule the president's objections. The opposition-dominated lower house overruled the veto in March.

Official results of the vote will be announced on Wednesday. Under the constitution, Yeltsin would have to sign the law within seven days. But Shvydkoi said the president would exercise his right of appeal to the Constitutional Court.

Yeltsin argued, when he vetoed the bill, that it breached international law, would complicate Russia's relations with many states and could prevent Moscow from recovering artworks taken from the Soviet Union during the war.

But many Russians, including members of parliament, view the art as legitimate compensation for the wartime suffering of the Soviet people and for the many Russian treasures destroyed during the German invasion.

"The deputies often vote with their heart and not according to what the law says. Civil servants do not have the right to act with their heart and I hope that they will understand that this law does not comply with the Russian constitution," said Shvydkoi, an art expert who is closely involved in the debate.
